title: FIx async search tests - do not warn on the presence of .async-search

timeline.body:
`.async-search` can sometimes appear if async request is slow, and there's no point for the test cleanup to complain about it. 

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/117099

timeline.message: FIx async search tests - do not warn on the presence of .async-search
timeline.author: Stanislav Malyshev

reply.body: Shouldn't we wait for those async requests then maybe? Is the index randomly popping up because we have those complete in the background somehow?

I think we should do both things. We should cancel any outstanding async requests and wait for them to die. I think folks have mostly been doing that in "after" clauses, but I feel like that's something we'd traditionally handle in the teardown code here.

But if the async-search index exists after the test we should trash it so we don't leak any async results from one test to another.

@original-brownbear I agree it may make sense to delete pending async searches when cleaning up the test, but I am not sure how to actually do it. It looks like each API (search, esql, etc) has its own async API and most of them don't even have "delete all" command or even "list all" command. So it seems to be a non-trivial thing to do. Any ideas how to do it? I'll create an issue to track it but I think this fix should not depend on it. Note that the index may pop up anytime the async request was long, regardless of having it finished or not by the time of the cleanup, so it's two separate things anyway.
I've made https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/117376 so we don't lose track of this concern.
